name: Qilin
description: Qilin (also tracked as Agenda) is currently the most active ransomware group by victim volume, maintaining over 100 incidents per month through mid-2026. Operates as a RaaS with an affiliate structure that insulates core operators from disruption. Victim count grew 14x in 2025 relative to 2024, totaling over 900 confirmed organizations.

ttps.notes: Primary initial access via VPN and edge device vulnerabilities
Frequently abuses stolen credentials for initial access
Rust/Go encryptors; WSL abuse to run Linux ELF encryptors on Windows

notable_techniques: WSL abuse to execute Linux ELF encryptors, bypassing EDR not configured for Linux binary detection
Post-RansomHub absorption â€” ~280% increase in victim disclosures
Intermittent/partial encryption for speed and evasion
detection_opportunities: WSL process spawning unusual child processes
Volume shadow copy deletion (vssadmin delete shadows)
PowerShell download cradles from unusual parent processes
response_playbook: Isolate affected hosts and check for WSL/Linux subsystem presence â€” Qilin deploys Linux ELF encryptors via WSL specifically to bypass EDR not configured for Linux binaries.
Hunt for vssadmin/wmic shadow copy deletion commands to determine how far the encryption stage has progressed.
Audit for unauthorized PsExec or SMB admin-share (ADMIN$/C$) activity from non-admin workstations indicating lateral movement.
Review PowerShell history for download cradles (IEX, Net.WebClient) used to stage the encryptor.
Preserve forensic images before remediation â€” Qilin's intermittent/partial encryption can leave recoverable data.
Audit and rotate credentials for any valid accounts used for initial access (T1190/T1078).
